_comment: Assertions the pinned corpus declares that the precompiled DuckDB store is
allowed to omit, each with the reason it is absent.
Why an allow-list rather than a tolerance: an assertion missing from the
store does not error, it simply never runs, and a report with a whole class
of assertion absent still reads as a healthy green run. That is how 200 AMT
assertions could be added to the corpus while BundledStoreMatchesCorpusTest
kept passing - it only checked that bundled assertions carried source hashes
and that there were more than 300 of them, never that the corpus declared
any the store lacked.
So the gate is: every assertion the corpus declares must be in the store,
unless it is named here with a reason. Unexplained absence fails the build.
Empty is the correct state. It was verified empty on 2026-09-07: the store
held exactly the 360 international assertions the corpus declared, with
nothing in the store that the corpus did not declare either.
Add an entry as "<uuid>": "<sqlFile> - <reason>". Reasons that would be
legitimate: a construct the publisher cannot port (gbTerm, usTerm and
caseSignificance need MySQL FULLTEXT plus RVF's res_* resource tables), or
an assertion that requires an input production never supplies. Note those
particular three ARE currently published and simply skip at runtime, which
is why they are not listed.
